item.title: 2026-03-16 Mouse PCLS Protocol 2.0
item.description:
Preparation one day before cutting, put filtered slicing buffer in -20 °C, take out the 2 nd day and keep it in 4 °C to have the slushie like texture, so that it can keep cold for a longer time in slicing chamber 1 hour before harvest: rewarm prepared 4% low melting agarose in 70 °C water bath Prepare slicing buffer in petri dish keep on wet ice
Assemble the blade (disinfect with 70% EtOH? ), set the cutting chamber at lowest position, fill the chamber outside with ice (Achtung: don‘t pack it too tightly, otherwise the chamber won’t be able to move down) , fill the chamber inside with filtered slushie like slicing buffer Autoclave and dry the surgery tools one day before
Prewarm the culture medium in 37 °C water bath According to Helen: pipette 1 mL per well in a 6-well-plate, also add sterile PBS to the spaces between the wells to maintain humidity, prewarm the well plates in 37 °C incubator (All procedures related to the culture medium are performed under the hood)
Harvest mouse liver
Wash the whole liver with PBS, then put it in another petri dish with slicing buffer Remove the gall balder with caution, CANNOT BREAK IT Separate the liver lobs Cutting with vibratome Take out the agarose form water bath, wait til good to use
Embed the liver lob in a 3.5 cm petri dish, put the liver lob in a proper position, then pour the agarose on it, wait until solidifies (according to JoVE Optimized and Simplified Technique for the Production and Culture of Precision-Cut Liver Slices pour in the agarose first, then put the lob into it) Use UHU Sekundenkleber to fix the agarose block with liver lob on a small black plate with magnet Put the small black plate in the chamber, adjust it to a position that is good for cutting, usually keep the liver lob vertical to the blade set the thickness at 250 um, cutting range, continuous mode, start discard the first slices, pick up the slices (liver slice and agarose slice whole piece together) carefully with square-tip forceps or spatula. Or according to Helen‘s protocol use a plastic Pasteur pipette with the tip cut halfway to create a wide opening so the slice can be aspirated, and then transferred into a Falcon tube or Petri dish containing slicing buffer for collecting PCLS)
Gentally sway the whole slice in slicing buffer in the 6 well plate until the liver part is fall off Discard the agarose without PCLS and also take out the agarose that floating in the cutting chamber for more space and next cutting process Use 4 mm biopsy stamp to cut the slices into same shape under the hood Transfer the slices under the hood into 6 well plate with 1 mL culture medium and 1 slice per well to culture Fix non-cultured fresh slices as internal control Put the 6 well plate on a orbital shaker in the incubator at 37 °C, with 7% CO_2 Take supernatant at every time point (0 1 2 3 6 24 48 72 96 120 144 168 in a week), store in -20 °C for LDH Assay For the first 3 h, take out the soup every hour, and take out the slice of the corresponding time point for fixation Then at 6h (,8h, 12h ideally), 24h and every time point, repeat the same process Problems unsolved how to deal with it after 1 week? when to add MASH Cocktail to induce? no analysis test for BA til now

item.title: 2026-02-12 mouse pcls protocol 1.0
item.description:
PCLS Protocol mouse 1.0 1 hour before harvest: rewarm prepared 4% low melting agarose in 70-80 °C water bath Prepare custodiol in petri dish and 6-well plate, keep on wet ice
Assemble the blade (disinfect with 70% EtOH), set the cutting chamber at lowest position, fill the chamber outside with ice, fill the chamber inside with slicing buffer Disinfect the tools with 70 % EtOH, harvest mouse liver, put in the Petri dish on ice Use scalpel to cut the liver block into a reasonable shape, normally rectangle, cut off the edge (need to be considered) Take out the agarose form water bath, wait til good to use Fix the shaped liver block on a small black plate with magnet 1-2 drops of glue on the plate, put a thin fabric layer on it Put the shaped liver block on it before the glue dry Put a metal ring around the block, pour melted agarose in it, wait til solified (Achtung! : don’t let the ring glued, otherwise it will take away the agarose) Take away the ring, cut off extra agar, careful not to cut the liver put the small black plate in the chamber, adjust it to a position that is good for cutting, usually vertical to the blade set the thickness at 250 um, cutting range, continuous mode, start discard the first 2-3 slices, pick up the slices (liver slice and agarose slice whole piece together) carefully with square-tip forceps or spatula Gentally sway the whole slice in custodiol in the 6 well plate until the liver part is fall off take out the agarose in well plate and also take out the agarose that floating in the cutting chamber for more space Put the comparable and intact slices in the same well, use for culture later
Meanwhile take out the prepared culture medium form the 4 °C fridge, and prewarm in 37 °C water bath take the 6 well plate with slices under the hood to transfer them into 12 well plate with 2 mL culture medium and 3-4 slices per well to culture, the wells are labeled with time points Fix and freeze non-cultured fresh slice as internal control put the 12 well plate on a orbital shaker in the incubator at 37 °C, with 7% CO_2 take supernatant for the first time point after 10-15 min in culture, store in -80 °C for LDH Assay for the first 3 h, take out the soup every 30 min, and take out the slices of the corresponding time point for fixation and freezing then at 6h (,8h, 12h ideally), 24h repeat the same process

Thereafter, they were transferred to another 12-well plate filled with 1.3 ml of three different media saturated with 80 %O2/5CO2: WME (with l-glutamine, Invitrogen, Paisly, Scotland) supplemented with 25 mM glucose and 50 mg/ml gentamycin (Invitrogen), RegeneMed® medium: WME supplemented with RegeneMed® additives (L3STA), antibiotics (L3MAB) and supplements (L3STS) in ratio 100:15.1:1:2.5 (RegeneMed®, San Diego, CA, USA) or Cellartis® Hepatocyte Maintenance Medium: WME supplemented with Cellartis® Hepatocyte Maintenance Medium Supplements (Cat. No. Y30051, Takara Bio Europe AB, Gothenburg, Sweden) and 50 mg/ml gentamycin. PCLS were incubated for 5 days with medium being refreshed daily.

item.title: IMG_0346
Pre-Think
item.description:
The maximum duration for which PCLS can maintain functional viability under in vitro culture conditions, (ideally up to two weeks).
Standardization of mouse strain selection and hepatic lobe sampling to improve the reproducibility of PCLS preparation.
Identification of viability and activity markers for PCLS beyond cleaved caspase 3.
Exploration of methodologies other than IHC and WB for assessing tissue viability and functional integrity.
Systematic benchmarking against the existing PCLS literature, including a consolidated summary of culture medium composition and critical operational parameters.
Establishment of a PCLS based experimental platform for MASH research, including the construction of a dedicated in vitro experimental unit and the overall experimental setup.

item.title: PCLS
item.description: Vibramote: Leica VT1000 SMethods Liver tissue was cored using a 8-mm Stiefel biopsy punch (Medisave, Weymouth, UK). Cores were transferred to a metal mould, submerged in 3% low geling temperature agarose (A9414; Sigma-Aldrich, Poole, UK), and placed on ice for 2-5 minutes. Agaroseembedded liver cores were superglued to the vibratome mounting stage, submersed in the media chamber containing 4°C Hank’s balanced salt solution+, and cut using a Leica VT1200S vibrating blade microtome (Leica Biosystems, Milton Keynes, UK) at a speed 0.3 mm/sec, amplitude 2 mm, and thickness (step size) of 250 μm (Fig. 1A). PCLSs were transferred onto 8-μm-pore Transwell inserts and cultured under static conditions in standard 12-well plates (Greiner Bio-One, Kremsmuenster, Austria) or in a modified tissue culture plate (BioR plate) and rocked on the bioreactor platform (patent PCT/GB2016/053310) at a flow rate of 18.136 μL/sec (Fig. 1B,C and Supporting Fig. S1A). For comparison, PCLS were cultured in Kirstall Quasivivo (qv500) units according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Supporting Fig. S1B). All PCLSs were cultured in Williams medium E (W4128; SigmaAldrich), supplemented with 1% penicillin/streptomycin and l-glutamine, 1× insulin transferrin-selenium X, and 2% fetal bovine serum (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cramlington, UK), and 100 nM of dexamethasome (Cerilliant, Texas, USA) at 37°C, supplemented with 5% CO2. Media were changed daily.
